 ** [[SQLITE_PREPARE_NO_VTAB]] <dt>SQLITE_PREPARE_NO_VTAB</dt>

intro_commit_message:
Enable SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS for FTS3, FTS5, and RTREE.

FossilOrigin-Name: f34c533b6c1f8ef3f69c75c1039406c12751cdde1fbdcb4d9776b24455facf8a
fix_commit_message:
Add the SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL flag to sqlite3_prepare_v3(). Use this to prevent fts3/4 tables in non-trusted schemas from calling unsafe SQL functions.

FossilOrigin-Name: 26f39ac806a5582fab1497e38a4ce68dad2b79df8c8aade43c4e21eed7576931
agent_reasoning: Without this change, FTS3/4 tables created in an untrusted schema (e.g. attached databases, or when SQLITE_DBCONFIG_TRUSTED_SCHEMA is off) could be used to indirectly invoke SQL functions flagged SQLITE_FUNC_DIRECT/SQLITE_FUNC_UNSAFE, because the module's own internally-generated SQL (built from schema-derived strings like column/table names and prepared as fresh top-level statements) was indistinguishable from trusted user SQL to the enforcement checks, which only recognized nested sub-parses (pParse->pToplevel!=0) or expressions parsed directly from DDL text (EP_FromDDL/fg.fromDDL). This let schema-controlled content smuggle calls to otherwise-restricted "unsafe" functions, defeating the purpose of marking FTS3/4 as SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS. The fix closes the gap by introducing SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL and having FTS3/4 set it on every internal sqlite3_prepare_v3() call via sqlite3Fts3PrepareStmt(), and by having the three risk-check sites also honor pParse->prepFlags & SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL, so these internal statements are now correctly subject to the trusted-schema restriction.
